problem: Open-vocabulary 3D scene graph generators (HOV-SG, ConceptGraphs) need well-aligned posed RGB-D image sequences, which are often missing for BIM or LiDAR point clouds. Room segmentation also struggles in complex scenes with unclear borders, and text-only LLM room typing fails when rooms contain few or common objects.
motivation: Robot navigation and language-grounded planning need hierarchical room/object scene graphs. Many real-world scans exist only as point clouds, and 3D-text paired data is scarce. Removing the posed-image dependency makes such graphs buildable from a point cloud alone.
key_idea: Build a room-object open-vocabulary 3D scene graph from a point cloud alone, by combining a border-enhanced density map with RoomFormer for room segmentation, rendering synthetic room snapshots for CLIP-based room typing (Snap-Lookup), and applying V-DETR proposals with Uni3D classification for objects.
insight: Adding visual CLIP features of synthetic room snapshots gives much better room typing than LLM inference from object lists. Table II: Ours mAP 0.69, versus 0.19 for GPT-4o on detected objects and 0.63 for GPT-4o/GPT-3.5 on GT objects. Border-enhanced density maps help RoomFormer as a pre-processing step (AP50 0.41 -> 0.53), and DBSCAN filtering of the cropped boxes improves point-cloud classification. No separate ablation isolates the DBSCAN effect.
method: Border-enhanced density map: slice the point cloud along z into N layers, project each to an occupancy grid, and drop layers whose free-space area falls outside [S/15, S*(1/15 or t)] bounds. Keep border cells present in at least 3/4 of the remaining layers, then blend with the density map: G = 0.9*G_den + 0.1*G_border.
Region detection: RoomFormer trained on Structured3D (3,000 scenes) and fine-tuned on 100 Matterport3D scenes segments the rooms.
Snap module: place cameras evenly on an elliptical trajectory around each room at the room-centre height, facing the centre, and snapshot the room views.

Lookup module: extract CLIP visual embeddings of the snapshots, distil them to K representative views by K-means, compute cosine similarity against CLIP text features, take the argmax for each view, and majority-vote the room type.

Object detection: V-DETR (pre-trained) generates class-agnostic 3D boxes on sampled room point clouds; each box is cropped and cleaned with DBSCAN to remove background points, then centred and normalized.
Object classification: Uni3D matches the filtered object point cloud to text embeddings for open-vocabulary labels, with no RGB-D alignment.

Voronoi navigation graph: project the free space within robot height, subtract the eroded map to get the boundary, build a Voronoi graph, then sparsify and trim it. A GPT-4 interpreter parses queries into room and object targets for hierarchical lookup.

setting.backbone: RoomFormer (fine-tuned) + CLIP + V-DETR (pre-trained) + Uni3D + GPT-4 query interpreter (frozen)
setting.training_data: RoomFormer trained on Structured3D (3,000 scenes) and fine-tuned on 100 MP3D scenes; V-DETR, CLIP and Uni3D are used pre-trained with no further training
setting.observation: 3D scene point cloud only (no posed RGB-D); LiDAR + camera on the real robot
setting.action_space: nodes on a Voronoi navigation graph (waypoint-based)
setting.simulator: none (static MP3D / ScanNetv2 datasets); real-world smart wheelchair
setting.privileged: none (a complete pre-built scene point cloud is required)

numbers.eval_set_note: 43 single-floor MP3D scenes not used for fine-tuning (from 189 single-floor scenes)

numbers_note: Real-world test reported only as 3 successes out of 5 queries; no other navigation benchmark. Metrics are printed as 0-1 fractions here.
results: Room segmentation on MP3D reaches AP50 0.53 and mIoU 0.59, beating RoomFormer (0.41/0.56) and HOV-SG (0.06/0.23). Room classification mAP is 0.69, beating GPT-4o with GT objects (0.63) and HOV-SG (0.19). On ScanNetv2 novel classes the method beats OpenIns3D on AP50 (0.38 vs 0.28 on 7 novel; 0.30 vs 0.29 on 17) without RGB-D. It is lower on AP25 for 17 classes (0.34 vs 0.39). The real-robot test succeeded on 3 of 5 queries.
limitations: The graph cannot distinguish multiple rooms or objects of the same type, so queries such as 'classroom' were ambiguous and caused both real-world failures.
The real-world navigation evaluation is tiny (5 queries, 1 building) and there is no standard navigation benchmark; the method also needs a complete pre-built scan.
Performance depends on off-the-shelf detectors; AP25 on 17 novel classes trails OpenIns3D.
